dek: Set for 27 September 2026 at the Xaysetha Economic Zone in Vientiane, Laos, this Green Step-organised half marathon offers three distances with registration open through RunLaos.com. A Mekong riverside race from a Lao social enterprise where the river and the cause share the spotlight.
verdict: The Mekong Half Marathon is a Vientiane road race organised by Green Step, a Lao social enterprise, at the Xaysetha Economic Zone along the Mekong River roughly 10 km from central Vientiane. Three distances (21K, 10K, 5K) with registration open through RunLaos.com. September is the tail of the rainy season: warm, humid, with the Mekong at its peak. The race online footprint is thin beyond Green Step social media, consistent with Laos emerging running market. For runners wanting a Lao half marathon with the Mekong River setting and social-enterprise character, this is a solid, bookable pick for 27 September 2026.

paragraphs: Vientiane is one of Southeast Asia most understated capitals, a low-rise city on the Mekong River with the Thai border visible across the water. The Xaysetha Economic Zone sits roughly 10 km southeast of the city centre along the Mekong, providing riverside roads and event infrastructure. The Mekong River rather than the venue architecture is the visual centrepiece of the race [1][2].
sections.heading: Vientiane and the Mekong

paragraphs: Green Step is a Lao social enterprise whose work spans environmental advocacy, community health, and sports-event organisation. The Mekong Half Marathon promotes active lifestyles in Laos while channelling resources toward Mekong causes. Expect a community-scale production rather than commercial polish [1].
sections.heading: Green Step: A Social Enterprise

paragraphs: The course runs through Xaysetha Economic Zone on flat roads parallel to the Mekong. Vientiane sits on the Mekong floodplain with negligible elevation gain, making this a PB-friendly profile. The Mekong in September is wide and powerful, with views across to the Thai bank giving the course an international-border quality unique among Southeast Asian road races [1][2].
sections.heading: The Course

paragraphs: September is the tail end of the Lao rainy season: 27-33C with humidity above 80 percent. Rain is a live possibility with 15-20 rainy days in September, though rain typically arrives as afternoon thunderstorms. The Mekong is at its annual peak, swollen with monsoon runoff. Train in hot conditions and hydrate at every station [3].
sections.heading: September Climate

paragraphs: Registration is currently open through RunLaos.com. Wattay International Airport (VTE) serves Vientiane with direct flights from Bangkok, Hanoi, and KL. The Xaysetha Economic Zone is a 20-minute tuk-tuk ride from the city centre. Confirm kit-collection details directly with Green Step before travelling [1].
sections.heading: Registration and Logistics

paragraphs: If you want a Mekong riverside half marathon with open registration and social-enterprise character, the Mekong Half Marathon is a solid pick for 27 September 2026. Accept the thin pre-race information and rainy-season risk, and register through RunLaos.com while the window remains open [1].
